subject: Rounding tolerance & prefix-credit apportionment for committed plan
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara@smartshelf.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rounding tolerance & prefix-credit apportionment for committed plan

Hi Lara —

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through SmartShelf's projected profile this morning. Two items came up that we flagged in the rest of the pricing packet and I wanted to clarify so we have the same expectations before the SOW sign: rounding tolerance for per-call billing and how prefix (KV cache) credits apportion across multi-tenant ingestion routes.

High level proposals from our side:
- Rounding tolerance: we apply a per-call rounding tolerance of 0.5 tokens when computing per-request meterization for streaming calls; monthly invoice aggregation uses the standard quantum (100 tokens) with a smoothing rule for bursts under 1k tokens. Practically, this reduces microcharges from telemetry noise but preserves accuracy for high-volume bursts.
- Prefix/KV credits: for committed capacity customers we provide a monthly pool of prefix credits tied to the committed tier. Credits are consumed first by exact route match then by prefix similarity; remaining credits are pro-rated to active ingestion routes based on 30-day token share.

I attached an example workbook with arithmetic for your January-November sample (sheet: "apportionment_walkthrough"). If the way we apportion credits looks risky for SmartShelf's split between Search and Summaries routes, we can change to a fixed allocation per route instead of a proportional pool.

Quick ask: could you confirm a) whether you prefer fixed allocations or pool + pro-rate; and b) if a 0.5 token rounding tolerance is acceptable or if you need stricter per-call precision for audit reasons?

Thanks — I copied Kim and Tessa to loop in Sales Ops and AE planning.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lara Chen <lara@smartshelf.io>

Subject: Re: Rounding tolerance & prefix-credit apportionment for committed plan

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the workbook. Quick answers are below, plus a couple of follow-ups from Billing: 

1) Rounding tolerance: Our compliance team prefers deterministic per-call accounting for auditability. Can you provide a variant that shows per-call accounting at native sub-token precision (for internal audit only) but still applies the smoothing for invoicing to reduce invoices noise? In short — show us the raw numbers and the post-smoothing invoice values.

2) Prefix credits: We like the pool model for flexibility, but we need to guarantee Search gets at least 60% of credits in off-peak months (historical usage skews heavy to Search during promos). Is there a way to add a minimum allocation floor per route in your pool model?

Attached is a CSV extract of our Jan-Nov usage (anonymized) for the two routes — should help with the apportionment math. Also, a heads up: procurement asked about acceptable rounding variance for the purposes of the SOW (they prefer a clear cap number).

I can hop on a short call if it's faster.

—Lara
Head of Platform Operations, SmartShelf
[attachment: sample-usage-jan-nov.csv (csv)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara@smartshelf.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, SmartShelf Billing <billing@smartshelf.io>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 12:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Rounding tolerance & prefix-credit apportionment for committed plan

Lara —

Appreciate the quick reply and the CSV. I ran two variants in the attached workbook:

A) Audit-raw: per-call token accounting at full precision (no rounding) exported to the audit sheet — useful for your compliance team.
B) Invoice-smooth: smoothing and invoice quantum applied at month-end with a hard cap on invoice variance of +/-0.3% vs raw (we can tighten that if procurement needs a lower cap).

For the prefix pool, I've added a "minimum-allocation" toggle in the workbook so you can set Search floor to 60% and the remaining credits will pro-rate across other routes. That will guarantee Search's minimum but still allow you to use surplus credits in heavier months.

Notes on tradeoffs: the floor approach increases the chance of unused credits on routes that dip, which would otherwise be available to other routes — happy to include an auto-transfer rule where unused floor credits convert to pool credits after a 7-day idle window.

Next steps I propose:
- Kim: can you confirm whether legal/procurement will accept invoice variance cap at +/-0.3%? If not, please propose the acceptable cap.
- Lara: if the 60% floor + 7-day auto-transfer looks OK, I will lock the wording in the pricing appendix and generate the SOW redline.

I've attached the updated workbook (sheet names: audit_raw, invoice_smooth, allocation_sim).

Best,
Priyom
[attachment: redwood_pricing_apportionment_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
